content.text:
**Clarity — Letter A.** A is easier to follow for a non-specialist on every structural measure. It opens by identifying exactly what is being reported on (all three accounts, named and numbered, managed to one model), so the reader never has to guess which money the numbers describe; B refers only to "the account" and never tells the reader the scope. A's bold section labels — Performance, What changed in the portfolio, A reduction in your fee — let a reader find the fee change without re-reading a wall of prose, whereas B delivers four undifferentiated paragraphs. A also glosses its jargon in place ("net of fees, that is, after the advisory fees you actually paid"), while B uses "net of fees," "gross return," and "net dividends" with no gloss at all. B has one genuinely confusing construction: "declined by -3.2%," a double negative that a careful reader has to stop and unpack. B is also missing the date and the firm/address block, which matter for a document clients will file alongside statements.

**Tone — Letter A.** The tone notes ask for precise, unhurried, no superlatives, for two analytical readers who go through attribution line by line. A states the portfolio return and the index return side by side and lets the readers draw the comparison themselves — exactly right for this audience. B editorializes: "This performance outperformed," "We are pleased to inform you," "We took advantage of market volatility," and a sentence of pure filler ("focused on navigating a challenging global environment while maintaining our long-term objectives") that conveys nothing and reads as marketing. For clients who will notice a rounding difference, unearned narrative flourish tends to erode rather than build confidence. B also frames the fee cut as a favor being bestowed ("As this is a benefit to you"); A states the mechanics and the effective date and leaves it there. A's closing offer to walk through the attribution is well-judged for readers described as reading attribution line by line; B ends with no such opening.

**Overall — Letter A.** This is not a length preference; B's extra words are filler, and A's advantage comes from structure, defined terms, and restraint. I would send A essentially as drafted.
